newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt yields excised report in immigration probe.
newsitem.headline: HK govt yields excised report in immigration probe.

text.p: Hong Kong's top civil servant on Thursday avoided a possible legal clash with legislators by delivering to them an excised version of a confidential report on former immigration chief Laurence Leung.

Legislators probing into Leung's removal had demanded that chief secretary Anson Chan deliver the report by the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) by Thursday and had hired a top British lawyer to determine if Chan would break the law by refusing.
"I made available an excised version of the ICAC Operations Review Committee Report to the Chairman of the Select Committee for his personal inspection alone," Chan said in a statement.

"Before doing so, I had obliterated from the report the sources of information, the names of persons, information pertaining to the operations of the ICAC and the comments, views and assessment, including legal advice, of the professionals concerned," she said.

Chan reiterated that the disclosure of the full report would have undermined public confidence in and the proper functioning of the ICAC, adding that disclosure of the excised report should not be taken as a precedent.
The report formed the basis of a government decision to force Leung to retire last July after investigators found he had undisclosed business ties.
